Portsmouth Direct line.subject: Indian Heritage

Portsmouth Direct line.fact: From a point just west of Cosham station to Portsmouth was jointly owned by the LSWR and the Brighton and Chichester Railway (soon to be LBSCR); the Brighton and Chichester Railway owned the line from Cosham Junction and Portcreek Junction back to Chichester; and from west of Cosham to Fareham belonged to the LSWR. Portsmouth Direct line.subject: Indian Heritage

Portsmouth Direct line.fact: The line from Chichester to Havant was opened on 15 March 1847; from Havant to Portsmouth on 14 June 1847; and from Farlington Junction to Cosham, for goods traffic, on 26 July 1848, and for passengers on 2 January 1860. From Portcreek Junction to Cosham Junction opened for goods on 1 September 1848, and for passengers on 1 October 1848.

Portsmouth Direct line.fact: These feelings were carried into the LBSCR, and marked tension now existed between the LSWR and the LBSCR.

Portsmouth Direct line.subject: Indian Heritage
Portsmouth Direct line.question: lxxxiii) on 26 June _____, to run from Epsom via Godalming to a Portsmouth terminus

Portsmouth Direct line.subject: Indian Heritage
Portsmouth Direct line.question: The Guildford to Godalming section (now part of the LSWR) opened on 15 October _____, after a delay when the tunnel at Guildford partly collapsed
Portsmouth Direct line.fact: The Guildford to Godalming section (now part of the LSWR) opened on 15 October 1849, after a delay when the tunnel at Guildford partly collapsed. The line closed again from 22 to 24 October 1849 from the same cause.

Portsmouth Direct line.subject: Indian Heritage

Portsmouth Direct line.fact: The Guildford to Godalming section (now part of the LSWR) opened on 15 October 1849, after a delay when the tunnel at Guildford partly collapsed. The line closed again from 22 to 24 October 1849 from the same cause.

Portsmouth Direct line.fact: The Portsmouth Railway got its authorising act, the Portsmouth Railway Act 1853 (16 & 17 Vict. xcix) on 8 July 1853, for a 32+1⁄4 mile route from Godalming (LSWR, at a junction just north of the original terminus) to Havant (LBSCR, on the line from Chichester to Portsmouth).

Portsmouth Direct line.fact: The Portsmouth Railway got its authorising act, the Portsmouth Railway Act 1853 (16 & 17 Vict. xcix) on 8 July 1853, for a 32+1⁄4 mile route from Godalming (LSWR, at a junction just north of the original terminus) to Havant (LBSCR, on the line from Chichester to Portsmouth).
